title: MTTR baseline + on-call toil measurement (Incident bot + diagnostics program)
content:
SHEET: MTTR baseline + on-call toil measurement
Owner: Aisha Bello (SLOs & paging metrics)
Primary audience: SRE + Eng leadership (Reliability Program)
Last refreshed: 2025-02-21
Coverage window: 2024-10-01 through 2025-01-31 (inclusive)
Incident sources: #incidents Slack threads + on-call timeline + incident doc (when present)
Services in scope: Hosted inference gateway, model-serving clusters, routing/control plane, telemetry (only when it impacts paging)

---
TAB: README (how to read this)
Goal of this sheet
- Establish a pre-project baseline for MTTR + responder toil, to compare against post-launch improvements from the incident bot “context bundles” + diagnostics standardization.
- Provide a weekly tracking template that SRE can update with minimal manual work.

Key outcome metrics tracked here (baseline + weekly)
- MTTR (minutes): time from “incident declared” to “resolved” (status updated to Resolved in the incident channel / incident doc).
- Time-to-first-action (TTFA, minutes): incident declared -> first documented mitigation or investigation action (e.g., rollback initiated, circuit breaker enabled, routing policy change, traffic shift, scaling action, query run with a concrete hypothesis).
- Time-to-suspect-change (TTSC, minutes): incident declared -> first mention of a plausible suspect deploy/config change with a link or identifier (PR, deploy event, config diff, rollout).
- Responder toil (minutes): estimated manual effort spent gathering context (deploy info, config snapshots/diffs, saturation dashboards, log/trace pivots) before the team lands on a primary hypothesis.
- Manual context queries (#): count of distinct “pull context” actions (examples below) prior to primary hypothesis.

What we mean by “toil” for this program (operational definition)
- Included (counted toward toil):
  - Manually looking up recent deploys/rollouts across services/regions (release dashboards, CI/CD logs, GitHub PRs, manual queries).
  - Manually diffing effective routing policy (feature flags, routing weights, rate limits, autoscaling knobs).
  - Manually checking saturation signals in multiple dashboards to determine if this is a capacity/scheduler issue.
  - Manually correlating change events with start time (copy/paste timestamps; “what changed in the last hour?” questions).
- Excluded (not counted as toil for this program):
  - Normal mitigation execution time once a clear action is chosen (e.g., waiting for rollback to complete).
  - Writing the postmortem.
  - Prolonged “monitoring while waiting” time.

Examples of “manual context queries” (how to count)
- 1 query = 1 unique, intentional context pull step, typically evidenced in Slack or in the incident doc timeline:
  - “Checking last deploy in us-east for inference-gateway…”
  - “Pulling current routing policy for /v1/chat…”
  - “Opening saturation dashboard for model-serving/us-east…”
  - “Searching logs for error spike start…”
  - “Checking canary rollout status…”
- If the same person refreshes the same dashboard repeatedly, count once unless they pivot to a different view (region/model/route).

Notes / limitations (baseline caveats)
- Many incidents don’t have a complete timeline; we used best-effort extraction from Slack timestamps and the on-call timeline.
- TTSC can be “N/A” for incidents where no change correlation was relevant (e.g., upstream cloud networking incident).
- Toil estimation has subjectivity; we used a consistent rubric and sample review with Rafael + Sean.
- Region attribution is “region impacted” (not necessarily where incident was detected first).

---
TAB: Definitions + Rubric
Field definitions
- Incident Type: primary classification (latency regression, elevated 5xx, elevated 429/throttling, partial outage, quality/correctness regression, control plane/routing misconfig, telemetry/pipeline issues).
- Region: us-east, us-west, eu-central, ap-southeast (match incident comms / impacted cluster).
- Severity: SEV0/SEV1/SEV2 (SRE internal).
- Declared_at: timestamp of “INCIDENT DECLARED” message in #incidents (or nearest equivalent).
- Resolved_at: timestamp of “RESOLVED” message or when incident status set to Resolved.
- Primary hypothesis time: timestamp when responders converge on a primary suspected cause (e.g., “this is likely caused by routing policy change X” or “this looks like GPU queue depth saturation”).

Toil scoring rubric (minutes)
- 0–5 min: context was already obvious (e.g., clearly correlated alert + obvious dashboard annotation; or a known ongoing provider outage).
- 5–15 min: some manual checks, but mostly straightforward.
- 15–30 min: responders manually stitched multiple sources (deploy + config + saturation) before landing on hypothesis.
- 30–60 min: scattered context, multiple false starts, unclear region/service mapping.
- 60+ min: high ambiguity or missing telemetry/change data; multiple handoffs.

Coding notes (for consistent weekly updates)
- If Declared_at is missing, use first “on-call engaged” timestamp.
- If Resolved_at is missing, use last message that confirms customer impact ended + rollback/mitigation completed.
- If TTSC doesn’t happen, record as blank and set TTSC_NA=TRUE.

---
TAB: Baseline Summary (aggregated)
Aggregation notes
- MTTR percentiles computed per incident type and region, across all severities unless noted.
- Incident count is number of incidents in the window with a clear declared/resolved timeline.
- Toil minutes shown as median (p50) and p75.

Latency regression | 22 | 41 | 68 | 112 | 6 | 18 | 17 | 28 | 6 | Often requires correlating saturation + recent change; deploy evidence inconsistently annotated
Elevated 5xx | 18 | 36 | 59 | 95 | 5 | 14 | 14 | 24 | 5 | Usually clear error spike but root cause often config/routing
Elevated 429/throttling | 16 | 52 | 88 | 140 | 7 | 22 | 23 | 35 | 7 | High saturation component; queue depth vs throttling hard to disambiguate quickly
Partial outage / availability | 9 | 63 | 104 | 171 | 8 | 20 | 26 | 44 | 8 | Handoffs common; mitigations sometimes traffic shift / regional failover
Quality/correctness regression | 6 | 74 | 126 | 210 | 9 | 35 | 31 | 55 | 9 | Often caught by customer reports; suspected change identification slower
Control plane / routing misconfig | 11 | 44 | 71 | 118 | 6 | 16 | 19 | 31 | 6 | Config diff is the missing early context; lots of “what changed?” loops
Telemetry/pipeline impacting paging | 5 | 28 | 45 | 70 | 4 | N/A | 10 | 18 | 4 | TTSC typically N/A; toil mostly in verification and disabling noisy alerts

TABLE: Baseline by region (all incident types)
Columns: Region | Incidents(n) | MTTR_p50 | MTTR_p75 | TTFA_p50 | TTSC_p50 | Toil_p50 | ManualQueries_p50 | Notes
us-east | 32 | 46 | 79 | 6 | 19 | 20 | 6 | Highest volume; change correlation hardest due to concurrent rollouts and busiest capacity
us-west | 19 | 38 | 66 | 5 | 15 | 16 | 5 | Generally cleaner deploy metadata; fewer concurrent changes
eu-central | 11 | 49 | 83 | 7 | 21 | 21 | 6 | Some missing saturation labels; dashboards not always region-filtered correctly
ap-southeast | 8 | 57 | 96 | 7 | 24 | 24 | 7 | More frequent cross-region escalations; time-zone handoffs inflate toil

SRE interpretation (baseline takeaways)
- TTSC is consistently ~15–25 minutes for the incident types we most want to improve (latency, 5xx, throttling, routing misconfig). This matches anecdotal feedback: responders spend the first 10–20 minutes gathering “what changed?” context.
- Toil is driven by three repetitive tasks: (1) recent deploy lookup (service+region), (2) routing/config snapshot + diff, (3) saturation snapshot across a handful of canonical panels.
- Regional variance suggests multi-region correctness + metadata consistency matter as much as bot formatting.

Data quality flags used in baseline detail
- TIMELINE_INCOMPLETE: missing declared/resolved; excluded from aggregates
- TTSC_NA: TTSC not applicable
- TOIL_ESTIMATED: toil derived from Slack evidence + rubric (most rows)

---
TAB: Weekly Tracking (template)
Purpose
- Simple weekly rollup for leadership reporting (Neha/Sean) and for detecting if the incident bot is moving leading indicators before MTTR shifts.

Cadence
- Update by end of day Monday for the prior week (Mon–Sun).
- Owner: SRE on-call program (Aisha primary; backup Rafael).

Leading indicators to track weekly (pre/post bot)
- Bot adoption: % of incidents with context bundle posted within 3 minutes.
- Bot performance: p50/p90 time-to-post; error rate by collector.
- TTSC: delta over baseline (primary target).
- Toil: delta over baseline (primary target).

Weekly update checklist
- [ ] Export list of incidents from #incidents (or incident tracker) for the week.
- [ ] For each incident, fill Declared_at/Resolved_at, then compute MTTR.
- [ ] Fill TTFA and TTSC using timeline evidence.
- [ ] Estimate toil minutes using rubric; count manual queries.
- [ ] If bot is enabled: record whether a context bundle was posted, time-to-post, and any missing sections.
- [ ] Add 2–3 qualitative notes for leadership: what improved, what still hurts, any redaction/restricted-mode issues.

---
TAB: Methodology (step-by-step)
How baseline was computed
1) Identify incidents in the window
   - Pull from #incidents channel history + incident index (where present).
   - Include SEV0/SEV1/SEV2 only.
2) Extract key timestamps
   - Declared_at: first clear incident declaration message.
   - Resolved_at: resolved message/status.
   - TTFA: first action message (mitigation or concrete investigation step).
   - TTSC: first message identifying a plausible deploy/config change with an ID/link.
3) Toil estimation
   - Review incident Slack thread for evidence of manual context gathering (deploy lookups, config fetches, saturation dashboard pivots).
   - Assign toil minutes based on rubric; record ManualQueries count.
4) QA
   - 10-incident spot check with Rafael + Sean for consistency.
   - Flag outliers for re-review.

Planned improvements (to reduce measurement effort)
- Once deploy/config annotation event schema is standardized, automate TTSC detection via linked events + incident start time overlap.
- When incident bot is live broadly, infer manual queries reduction from reduced “asking for context” messages + fewer dashboard pivots.

Open questions
- Should TTSC be measured as “suspect change identified” or “suspect change confirmed”? (Current: identified; confirmation can be much later.)
- For incidents spanning multiple regions, should TTSC be per-region or just first suspect change anywhere? (Current: per incident; region impacted is the primary one.)
- How to handle “restricted mode” incidents in weekly metrics reporting without leaking details? (Plan: aggregate-only, no incident IDs.)
